'''Giant rats''' are low level vermin. These are often fought by low level players because of their low combat level, accessibility, and their drops of bones and [[raw rat meat]], which can be cooked over a fire and consumed to restore [[life points]].

==Update history==
{{UH|
* {{UL|type=update|update=Patch Notes: Part 2 - Combat Style Modernisation|date=2 March 2026}}
** Default base hit chances increased:
*** Magic ('weak'): 65 → 70
*** Melee ('same'): 55 → 60
*** Ranged ('strong'): 45 → 50

* {{UL|type=update|update=Patch Notes: Early-Game Rebalance|date=16 February 2026}}
** Giant rats in [[Lumbridge Swamp]] have been reduced in combat prowess:
*** Life points reduced to 1100 (from 1450)
*** Maximum hit reduced to 40 (from 100)
*** Armour reduced to 110 (from 150)
*** Defence level reduced to 2 (from 5)
*** Attack level reduced to 4 (from 5)
*** Removed healing effect (formerly healed 1 life point per tick)
** Level 7 rats which were impaled by arrows have mostly had the model replaced with arrowless versions.

* {{UL|type=patch|update=MHAW & Double XP - This Week In RuneScape|date=15 May 2023}}
** Updated models for [[skeleton]]s, [[zombie]]s and giant rats within the [[Wilderness]], giving them the new [[Unwelcome Guests]] models.

* {{UL|type=update|update=Runescape beta is now online!|date=4 January 2001}}
** Added to game.
}}

==Trivia==
* Giant rats are one of the few [[RuneScape]] [[monsters]] that blink.
* On [[Tutorial Island]], a [[player]] would have to kill a giant rat.
* Usually the low level giant rats have light fur while the higher levels have dark fur.
* Partly decomposed corpses of giant rats can be seen in some of the puddles in Lumbridge Swamp.
* The giant rats in the low-level [[Wilderness]] are aggressive to players.
* In [[Betrayal at Falador]], the characters [[Theodore]] and [[Castimir]] reminisce that the children of [[Rimmington]] would hunt giant rats for fun using rocks and arrows. Despite their size, they were apparently too clumsy and stupid to be a threat.{{CitePub |author=T.S. Church |title=Betrayal at Falador |pages=252 |publisher=Titan Books |pubyear=2010 (edited rerelease)|notes="They laughed at remembrances of the giant rats that lived to the east of Rimmington where they had grown up. Although the size of a pig, the animals had been uncommmonly stupid and clumsy. Hunting them with rocks or arrows had been a frequent hobby of children.}}
